-73.95520,40.76550.name: Weill Cornell Medicine, Center for Reproductive Medicine
-73.95520,40.76550.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Zev Rosenwaks, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-122.03635,37.36883.name: Comparative Biosciences, Inc.
-122.03635,37.36883.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Genesis Biotechnology Group. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.92307,52.46928.name: Care Fertility Birmingham
-1.92307,52.46928.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

85.32000,27.68000.name: Nepal Agricultural Research Council
85.32000,27.68000.desc: Nepal spans lowland plains to high mountains and holds landraces adapted across that whole range, which is an unusual concentration of climate adaptation in one small country. Its collections matter well beyond its borders for exactly that reason.

-73.46800,40.86000.name: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory
-73.46800,40.86000.state: Cold Spring Harbor, New York — 1 Bungtown Road
-73.46800,40.86000.desc: Where the 1975 Asilomar-era conversations about recombinant DNA were shaped and where a great deal of foundational molecular biology was done. It is also the institution whose earlier history included the Eugenics Record Office, which is part of the same building's record and part of why arguments about human genetics carry the weight they do.

-73.56700,45.50350.name: Biosafety Clearing-House — decisions and consultations
-73.56700,45.50350.desc: Every party to the Cartagena Protocol must file its decisions here, and for most first imports intended for release a public consultation is required before that decision is taken. For countries with no national notice venue of their own, this is the only place an application becomes visible in advance. It is also where to check what a neighbouring country has decided about the same organism.

-93.64030,42.01420.name: USDA Center for Veterinary Biologics
-93.64030,42.01420.desc: The US regulator for veterinary vaccines, and the body that created the prescription platform category in 2018. Its handling of the dairy cattle H5N1 question shows what such a regulator actually weighs: the virus is classified highly pathogenic, so testing required a containment level demanding three barriers and showering in and out, until a 2024 notice allowed studies outside containment facilities and shortened the path. Against that sat a trade consideration named openly by the developers — international agreements could penalise dairy products from vaccinated animals. A vaccine decision here is simultaneously a biosafety judgement, a laboratory-capacity question and an export negotiation, and the last of those is rarely visible in any register.

-77.03650,38.89770.name: US Fish and Wildlife Service — Office of Law Enforcement
-77.03650,38.89770.desc: The agency that clears or refuses live-animal imports at the US border, and the reason the laboratory primate trade changed shape after 2022. Following the indictment of a Cambodian supplier's officers, it declined to clear Cambodian shipments without incontrovertible evidence that the animals were purpose-bred. The largest US contract research organisation, which had sourced around 60 per cent of its primates from Cambodia, suspended imports and warned investors of a two to four hundred basis point hit to revenue growth; a competitor that had taken $140 million from Cambodian monkeys in 2022 lost most of its market value in a week. The industry has since been working on genetic testing to prove captive breeding — which is an admission that the paperwork never could.
